concept: Banner is a strip of the case set into the flow at the top of a screen that says in a printed glyph and a word what condition holds, and stays there until the condition ends.

default_to_avoid.pattern: inline notification banner with a coloured stripe on the start edge, a tinted background and a bold title over muted body (Carbon inline notification)
default_to_avoid.why_not: The stripe and the tint tell status by colour and paint a second loud part, which P1 forbids and the habit gate G-X1 flags.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material banner with a tinted icon disc, two text buttons and a full width rule under it
default_to_avoid.why_not: The tinted disc is the alert habit G-X1 flags, and two text buttons give a message two loud answers when it needs at most one key.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): labels printed beside each control, never inside a coloured badge
Braun HF 1 television (Dieter Rams, 1958): one band of printing across the case that says what the set is doing
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Alert pattern and WCAG 2.2 4.1.3 Status Messages

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: No tone is orange; the glyph takes the tone's mark ink and the action key is a plastic Button, so the screen's orange key stays its own.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only; hierarchy by size and position
derivation.form: The status word is type.label in medium weight before the message in regular weight; no bold title, no muted body.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes; no tinted text
derivation.form: The body stays the plastic of the case in every tone; only the glyph's shape and the word tell the tone.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The banner takes a fixed place at the top of the region it speaks for and does not slide in; it is there for as long as the condition is.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The action key is a 44px Button and the dismiss key a 44px round IconButton.

options.name: strip of the case, a plastic band at unit height in the flow
printed line on the page with a seam under it
engraved plate, the words in a recessed well

variants.reason: A stands off the page as its own short body so a condition that blocks controls is seen first, while staying plastic in every tone (P1, P5); B sinks into the page text and C adds a second recess that competes with the display window (P2) and reads as a field.

root.why: The strip is a body at unit height with a short shadow, never floating higher than a card.

head.why: Glyph and status word sit together at the start of the inset line, printed before the message.

glyph.why: The glyph is printed flat in stroke ink with no disc behind it and no emboss.

status.why: The status word is medium weight at label size, so the tone has a word as well as a shape.

message.why: The message stays in the primary ink at 4.5:1 on the plastic in every tone.

keys.why: The action and dismiss keys sit together at the inline end, where the hand expects them.

neutral.why: A neutral note prints a ring glyph in the info mark ink, with the plastic body unchanged.

positive.why: A condition that is good prints the tick glyph in the positive mark ink, body unchanged.

warning.why: A warning prints the triangle glyph in the primary ink, because amber on plastic falls under 3:1.

critical.why: A failure prints the octagon glyph in the critical mark ink and the word says what failed.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the strip keeps a real border and the glyph takes the text colour.
